_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Japan covering Jōmon and Yayoi periods, Yamato state, Nara and Heian courts, samurai rise, Kamakura/Muromachi/Sengoku periods, Tokugawa shogunate, Meiji Restoration, imperial expansion, Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese wars, WWI, militarism, WWII (Pearl Harbor, Hiroshima/Nagasaki), US occupation, economic miracle, bubble economy, Lost Decades, Fukushima 2011, and contemporary Japan.

religion.note: Many Japanese practise both Shinto and Buddhism simultaneously (syncretic); New Religions (Soka Gakkai, Tenrikyo); Christmas culturally celebrated; low religiosity in daily life

ethnic_groups.name: Japanese (Yamato)
ethnic_groups.notes: Japonic language; highly homogeneous; strong cultural identity; Yamato as dominant ethnic identity since Kofun period

ethnic_groups.name: Ainu
ethnic_groups.notes: Indigenous people of Hokkaido (also formerly Sakhalin, Kurils); recognised as indigenous 2019; distinct language (critically endangered); ~25,000 self-identified; historically marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Ryukyuan/Okinawan
ethnic_groups.notes: Okinawa and Ryukyu Islands; Ryukyuan languages (related to Japanese); formerly independent Ryukyu Kingdom (1429-1879); US-administered 1945-1972; US bases remain; distinct culture

ethnic_groups.name: Korean (Zainichi)
ethnic_groups.notes: ~450,000; colonial-era labourers and descendants; North/South Korean community divide; discrimination; many adopted Japanese names; Chongryon (pro-DPRK) and Mindan (pro-ROK)

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest foreign nationality (~800,000); historical communities plus new arrivals; students and workers

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Brazilian, Filipino, Vietnamese, Nepali)
ethnic_groups.notes: Brazilian (~210,000; Nikkei returnees); Vietnamese (~520,000; technical trainees); Filipino (~310,000); Burakumin (socially discriminated historic outcast group, ~1-3M, ethnically Japanese)

independence.notes: Continuous sovereignty; National Foundation Day February 11 (660 BC mythical); modern constitution 1947 under US occupation; sovereignty restored 1952 (Treaty of San Francisco)

country_profile.notes_unique: World's oldest continuous monarchy; 3rd-largest economy; aging/shrinking population (critical); anime/manga cultural soft power; only country to have suffered nuclear attacks; 47 prefectures; emperor is national symbol

geography.terrain: Mountainous archipelago (6,852 islands); volcanic; 73% forested; narrow coastal plains
geography.notes: Ring of Fire (111 active volcanoes); world's most seismically active country; 2011 Tōhoku earthquake/tsunami/Fukushima; four main islands (Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu, Shikoku); 6th largest EEZ globally.

economy_extended.notes: World's 4th largest economy; lost decades (1991-2010) stagnation; Abenomics; yen weakness (2022-24); automotive giant (Toyota largest global automaker); robotics leader; world's largest government debt-to-GDP ratio (260%+); aging population economic challenge.

health.notes: World's highest life expectancy (84+ years); universal healthcare since 1961; highest hospital beds per capita globally; aging society (29% over 65); mental health/suicide concerns; Okinawa blue zone.

food_agriculture.notes: Only 37% food self-sufficiency (calorie basis, lowest among major economies); rice staple (declining consumption); Wagyu beef globally premium; calorie-based food self-sufficiency declining; fisheries historically important (whaling controversy).

energy.notes: World's #1 LNG importer; Fukushima disaster (2011) led nuclear shutdown — slow restart (33 of 54 reactors decommissioned); aggressive hydrogen strategy; 46% GHG reduction target by 2030; solar expansion rapid; ocean/tidal energy research.

transport.notes: Shinkansen (bullet train) since 1964 — zero fatalities; world's most punctual rail system; Tokyo Metro world's busiest; new maglev line (Chuo Shinkansen, 500 km/h) under construction; automotive nation (Toyota, Honda, Nissan).

tourism.notes: Record 31.9M visitors in 2023 (pre-pandemic record broken); weak yen driving tourism boom; overtourism in Kyoto; anime/manga pilgrimage tourism; cherry blossom season; food tourism (most Michelin stars globally); onsen culture.

legal_system.notes: 1947 Constitution (drafted under US occupation); Article 9 renounces war (reinterpreted for self-defense); 99.9% conviction rate (prosecutor-driven system); Emperor purely ceremonial; Liberal Democratic Party dominated since 1955.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Legal (some local partnership certificates; no national marriage)
human_rights_gender.notes: Strong democracy; persistent gender gap (lowest women in STEM among OECD; 'womenomics' policies); homogeneous society (2% foreign residents, rising); death penalty retained (hanging); press club system (kisha clubs) limits press freedom.

security_stability.notes: Among world's safest countries; Article 9 pacifist constitution but increasing militarization (2022 security strategy revision — 2% GDP defense target); US-Japan alliance cornerstone; China/North Korea threats; Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands dispute.

cultural_heritage.notes: Anime/manga $25B+ industry (global soft power); most Michelin-starred city (Tokyo); samurai/bushido cultural heritage; tea ceremony (sado); ikebana flower arrangement; wabi-sabi aesthetic philosophy; Nintendo/Sony/Pokémon global impact.

comparative_rankings.notes: World's 4th largest economy; top soft power globally (anime/cuisine/technology); peace rankings among best; gender gap worst in G7; aging/declining population major challenge.
comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.
